cases.subject: AX4102: welcome, schedule and course materials
cases.body: Dear students, welcome to AX4102 Applied AI Systems. I hope the first weeks of the semester are going well. This message collects several practical details that were also mentioned during orientation, so please keep it for reference. Our regular class is on Thursday evenings from 18:30 to 21:30 in Studio B. The room has movable tables because some sessions will include group design work rather than a standard lecture. The course site is now open, and you should be able to find the handbook, the Topic 1 slide deck, and the full team-project brief in the Resources section. Please read these materials before our first class so that we do not need to spend the session reviewing administrative information. We will run a short hands-on exercise during the second half of class, so bring a charged laptop and make sure you can connect to campus Wi-Fi. A phone or tablet will not be suitable for all parts of the exercise. If you cannot access the course site, contact the learning-platform help desk rather than replying to the whole class. I look forward to meeting everyone on Thursday.
cases.summary: AX4102 meets Thursdays from 18:30–21:30 in Studio B. Review the handbook, Topic 1 slides, and team-project brief before class, and bring a laptop for the lab.

expected.action: Review the handbook, Topic 1 slides, and team-project brief before class

cases.subject: AX4102 team project: proposal requirements
cases.body: Hello AX4102 teams, the proposal submission area for the semester project is now available. The proposal is intended to show that your group has selected a clear problem and has thought carefully about how the project could be evaluated; it is not expected to be a finished technical design. Please submit one document for the whole team rather than separate individual files. The main text should be no more than two pages and should explain the problem you want to address, the intended users, the data you plan to use, the success metrics you will track, the main risks or limitations, and the responsibilities of each team member. References may be included at the end, but please keep the discussion focused and readable. Convert the document to PDF and use a filename that includes your team name. Only one member needs to upload it, but every member should check that the final version is correct. The submission deadline is 23:59 on 4 October 2026. The portal records the final uploaded file, so replacing a draft before the deadline is allowed. Late files will need approval from the teaching team. Questions about project direction should be posted in the course forum so that the answers are visible to all teams.
cases.summary: Submit one two-page AX4102 team proposal PDF covering the problem, users, data, metrics, risks, and responsibilities by 23:59 on 4 October 2026.

expected.action: Submit the AX4102 two-page team proposal as one PDF

cases.subject: AX4102 proposal deadline extended and rubric clarified
cases.body: Dear AX4102 students, thank you for the questions raised during yesterday's consultation. Several teams explained that the original proposal window was difficult because it overlapped with another programme submission. After discussing this with the teaching team, we have decided to extend the proposal deadline. Please note that the new deadline is 18:00 on 6 October 2026, replacing the earlier deadline of 23:59 on 4 October. The learning platform has already been updated, so you do not need to request an individual extension. We have also clarified the format after seeing that some teams were struggling to fit diagrams and evaluation tables into two pages. The proposal may now be up to three pages, excluding references. This is a maximum, not a target, and clear writing is still preferred. For transparency, the marking rubric will place 40% on the quality of your reasoning, 30% on evaluation design, 20% on feasibility, and 10% on presentation. In particular, a long feature list will not replace a clear explanation of why your chosen approach is suitable. If your team has already submitted, you may leave the existing file or upload a revised version before the new deadline. The most recent file in the portal will be marked.
cases.summary: The AX4102 proposal is now due at 18:00 on 6 October 2026 and may be three pages excluding references. The required action is to update and submit it using the clarified 40/30/20/10 rubric.

expected.action: Update the AX4102 proposal to the clarified rubric and submit by the extended deadline

cases.subject: Submission received: AX4102 team proposal
cases.body: This is an automated confirmation from the AX4102 learning platform. The submission was made before the revised deadline and has been added to the teaching team's marking queue. Your confirmation reference is AX4-7K2M; please keep this reference in case you need to report a technical issue. The platform has completed its basic file check and was able to open the PDF. You do not need to upload the document again or email a copy to the instructor. No further action is required unless a member of the teaching team contacts your group directly. cases.subject: Project NOVA kickoff and ownership
cases.body: Hi Alex and Sam, thanks for joining the Project NOVA kickoff this morning. I am writing down the decisions while they are still fresh because our notes covered several possible directions. For this sprint, NOVA will be a prototype email-triage assistant aimed at student project teams who receive course notices, task updates, and administrative messages across different accounts. We agreed that the prototype should help a user understand what needs attention without pretending to replace the original inbox. To avoid overlapping work, Alex will own retrieval and source citations, including the logic that selects useful email evidence. Sam will own the user interface and the path from the dashboard to message details. I will own the evaluation plan, test cases, and final results review. We can help each other, but please keep these owners updated when making changes in their area. The first checkpoint is scheduled for 15:00 on 29 September. At that meeting, each owner should show working progress, explain one current risk, and identify any dependency that could block the final demo. A polished presentation is not needed yet. Please add short updates to the shared project board before the meeting so that we can spend the call making decisions rather than collecting status reports.
cases.summary: Project NOVA is an email-triage prototype. Alex owns retrieval and citations, Sam owns the interface, and Priya owns evaluation; prepare an update for 15:00 on 29 September.

expected.action: Prepare the Project NOVA retrieval and citation checkpoint update

cases.subject: Project NOVA: scope decision and demo scenario
cases.body: Hi team, here is a written record of the scope decisions from today's NOVA review. We discussed whether the demo should focus on one deeply integrated mailbox or show how the same workflow handles messages from several sources. The group agreed that the second option better demonstrates the original problem, so the demo should represent Gmail, Outlook, and a university mailbox that is automatically forwarded into Gmail. The sender shown in the product must still be the original sender, not the student who owns the forwarding account. For the public dataset, we will use exactly 20 synthetic messages with fictional names, addresses, courses, and organisations. Some messages should belong to the same topic so that the knowledge and question-answering features can be demonstrated. We are not building calendar write-back in this sprint. Calendar events may be detected and displayed, but the product must not create or edit an external calendar. The main cross-email demo question will be: what remains to be done for the AX4102 proposal? This scenario should include an initial requirement, a later deadline change, and a final submission receipt. Please treat these points as the agreed scope unless the team records a new decision.
cases.summary: NOVA will demo Gmail, Outlook, and forwarded university mail using 20 synthetic messages. Calendar write-back is deferred; the main question covers the AX4102 proposal.

expected.decision: Use three mailbox sources and 20 synthetic messages; defer calendar write-back

cases.subject: Project NOVA evaluation review: three gaps
cases.body: Hi team, I completed the first structured review of the Project NOVA evaluation results. The overall workflow is understandable, but three issues could reduce trust during the release review. First, questions containing a clear identifier sometimes retrieve high-scoring but unrelated messages. For example, a question about a course code can include a product newsletter simply because both emails contain common AI terms. Second, processing the same message more than once can create duplicate action items in some paths. This makes the dashboard counts look unreliable even when the underlying email has not changed. Third, subscription announcements are sometimes treated as actions, even when they only describe a renewal or new feature and do not require a user decision. Please add a focused regression case for each problem before release: identifier retrieval should exclude irrelevant sources, reprocessing should be idempotent, and informational subscriptions should stay out of the action list. It would also be helpful to preserve the failing behaviour and the corrected result in the engineering notes. These are the priority gaps from this review; minor visual issues can wait until the data behaviour is stable.
cases.summary: NOVA has three evaluation gaps: irrelevant identifier retrieval, duplicate actions after reprocessing, and informational subscriptions in the action list. Add regression tests for all three.

expected.action: Add regression tests for retrieval precision, action idempotency, and subscription exclusion

cases.subject: Project NOVA release review package and deadline
cases.body: Dear Project NOVA team, this message confirms the release-review package and schedule. The stakeholder review will take place on 9 October 2026 according to the agenda shared separately. Before the session, please place the release candidate in the internal delivery workspace so reviewers can start it without requesting additional access. The package must include the tagged source archive, deployment manifest, concise runbook, configuration template with no secrets, synthetic sample data, and the latest regression and model-quality results. Add a short release note that lists the supported workflow, known limitations, rollback procedure, and the owner for each unresolved risk. The release candidate must remain read-only against external email systems during review. All package materials are due by 12:00 on 8 October 2026. Minor fixes may continue after the upload, but any replacement must use a new version tag and explain the change. The version available at the deadline will be used for the stakeholder review on 9 October.
cases.summary: Deliver the tagged NOVA release candidate, deployment manifest, runbook, safe configuration template, synthetic data, quality results, and release notes by 12:00 on 8 October 2026; stakeholder review is 9 October.

expected.action: Deliver the NOVA release package with runbook, configuration, data, quality results, and release notes

cases.subject: New sign-in to your demo account — SEC-4821
cases.body: Hello, we recorded a new sign-in to your demo account and are sending this message so that you can confirm whether the activity was expected. The sign-in occurred at 07:02 on 1 October 2026 using Chrome on macOS. The approximate location was Singapore; location estimates can be affected by mobile networks, corporate routing, or privacy services, so the city alone may not identify the user. The activity reference is SEC-4821. If you signed in on this device, you do not need to take any action and you may keep this email for your records. If you do not recognise the sign-in, open the official account page by typing its known address or using your saved bookmark. Review recent account activity, sign out unfamiliar sessions, and change your password. Do not send your password or one-time code by email. Our support team will never ask for payment details to resolve a sign-in alert. This notification was generated automatically, so replies to this address are not monitored.
cases.summary: Chrome on macOS signed in from Singapore at 07:02 under reference SEC-4821. Take no action if recognised; otherwise review activity and change the password through the official site.

expected.conditional_action: Review SEC-4821 only if the sign-in is unfamiliar

cases.subject: URGENT: mailbox suspension — verify within 30 minutes
cases.body: FINAL SECURITY WARNING: our automatic system has detected an unpaid mailbox validation charge and your account is now marked for permanent removal. Previous notices may have been filtered into spam, which is why this is the last message you will receive. To prevent deletion, you must complete verification within 30 minutes. Open http://account-verify.invalid/login and enter your current email password, mobile number, and payment-card information so that the system can confirm account ownership. A small temporary charge may appear and will be returned after verification. Do not close the page while the security check is running. If the page does not load, reply directly to this email with your username and the one-time code sent to your phone; our verification agent will enter it for you. Failure to complete every step immediately will remove stored messages, cloud files, and contacts without recovery. This process cannot be completed through the normal account settings because your account is already in the suspension queue. Act now to keep access.
cases.summary: Quarantined phishing message demanding a password, one-time code, and payment card through an untrusted domain under an urgent deletion threat.

cases.subject: CloudNotes Pro renewal on 15 October
cases.body: Hello, this is a routine reminder about your CloudNotes Pro subscription. Your current monthly plan is scheduled to renew automatically on 15 October 2026 at the existing price of USD 12 per month. The renewal will use the payment method already saved in your account, and your notes, shared workspaces, and current storage allowance will continue without interruption. No action is required if you want to keep the plan. You can review invoices, change the payment method, move to the free plan, or cancel renewal from the Billing section of the official account settings before the renewal date. Cancelling stops the next charge but does not immediately remove access to features already paid for during the current billing period. Taxes may appear separately depending on the billing address. This message does not announce a price increase and does not require a reply. For security, customer support cannot change billing details by email. If you recently changed or cancelled the plan, the account page contains the most current status and can be used instead of this reminder.
cases.summary: CloudNotes Pro will renew automatically for USD 12 per month on 15 October 2026. No action is needed to continue; changes or cancellation are available in account settings.

cases.subject: CloudNotes Pro now includes meeting summaries
cases.body: Hello CloudNotes Pro member, we are sharing a product update following several months of testing with small teams. Automatic meeting summaries and calendar sync are now included in your existing Pro plan. Meeting summaries can create a draft recap from imported notes, highlight decisions, and collect follow-up items in one page. Calendar sync can display upcoming events beside related notebooks, but it will remain off until you enable it in Integrations. These features are being released gradually, so they may appear at different times across desktop and mobile applications. No plan upgrade is required, and there is no additional charge. Your current monthly price and renewal date stay the same. Existing privacy controls also remain available; administrators of shared workspaces can decide whether meeting-summary features are allowed for their members. This is an informational product announcement, not a request to change settings. If you do not want to use the new features, you can simply leave them disabled. Release notes and setup guidance are available in the Help Centre.
cases.summary: CloudNotes Pro now includes optional meeting summaries and calendar sync at no extra cost. The price and renewal date are unchanged, and no action is required.

cases.subject: CloudNotes payment failed — update by 18 October
cases.body: Hello, we were unable to complete the scheduled renewal for your CloudNotes Pro subscription because the saved payment method was declined. We will make one additional automatic attempt, but access to paid features will become read-only after 18 October 2026 if payment is not completed. Your existing notes will not be deleted on that date, and you will still be able to view or export them, but editing, premium meeting summaries, and additional uploads may be unavailable. If you want to keep Pro, sign in through the official CloudNotes website or app and update the payment method in Account Settings under Billing. Please do not send card information by email. You may also choose to take no action and allow the workspace to move to read-only mode. If you update payment successfully, the account page should show the new status immediately and no reply is needed. This notice relates only to the CloudNotes Pro subscription; it does not affect unrelated services or your email account. Contact support through the in-app Help section if the billing page shows a successful payment but access is still limited.
cases.summary: CloudNotes renewal failed. Update the payment method through official settings by 18 October 2026 to keep Pro, or allow the account to become read-only.

expected.action: Update the CloudNotes payment method or allow the plan to become read-only

cases.subject: Helio Robotics graduate engineering talk
cases.body: Dear students, the Careers Office will host an employer information session with Helio Robotics for anyone interested in engineering, software, or applied AI roles after graduation. Representatives from the company's autonomy and manufacturing teams will introduce the 2027 graduate engineering programme, describe the first-year rotation structure, and share examples of projects completed by recent graduates. There will also be time for questions about technical interviews, relocation, and the skills the company looks for in student projects. The talk will take place on 12 October 2026 from 16:00 to 17:00 in Career Studio 2. Registration is optional, but it helps us plan seating and allows us to send any last-minute room update. The registration form closes on 10 October. Attending the talk is not required in order to apply for a role, and registering does not create an application. Students from any programme may attend if they are interested. Please bring your student card for building access. A recording is not currently planned, but presentation slides may be shared afterward if the speakers approve.
cases.summary: Helio Robotics will present its 2027 graduate engineering programme on 12 October, 16:00–17:00, in Career Studio 2. Optional registration closes 10 October.

cases.subject: Helio Robotics applications close 20 October
cases.body: Hello students, following last week's employer session, Helio Robotics has opened applications for its 2027 graduate software engineering and applied AI positions. The roles are suitable for final-year students and recent graduates with experience in areas such as machine learning, backend systems, robotics, data engineering, or human-computer interaction. Previous robotics experience is welcome but is not required for every team. Applications must be submitted through the university careers portal by 23:59 on 20 October 2026. The required materials are a current CV, an unofficial or official academic transcript, and a project summary of no more than 200 words. The project summary should explain one technical project, your own contribution, and what you learned; it does not need to be related to robotics. Cover letters and reference letters are not requested at this stage. Candidates selected for the next round will receive a separate invitation for an online technical discussion. This message is an opportunity notice rather than a course requirement, so there is no academic penalty for not applying. Please direct portal problems to the Careers Office rather than the employer.
cases.summary: Helio Robotics graduate software and AI applications close at 23:59 on 20 October 2026. Submit a CV, transcript, and 200-word project summary through the careers portal.

cases.subject: Invitation: Responsible AI roundtable
cases.body: Hello Alex, we would like to invite you to a small Responsible AI roundtable bringing together researchers, product teams, public-sector staff, and student project leads. The discussion will focus on practical ways to document model limitations, communicate uncertainty, and evaluate systems that make recommendations from personal or organisational data. This is intended to be a working conversation rather than a formal conference panel, so participants will be invited to share examples and questions from their own projects. The roundtable is scheduled for 14 October 2026 from 14:00 to 16:00 in Harbour Room 3. Light refreshments will be available from 13:45, and the discussion will begin promptly at 14:00. Attendance is free, but seating is limited. Please reply to this email by 9 October to let us know whether you plan to attend. If you have accessibility or dietary requirements, you may include them in the reply. A full paper or presentation is not required, although you are welcome to bring brief notes. We will send a final reminder and any room update to confirmed participants.
cases.summary: Reply by 9 October if you will attend the Responsible AI roundtable on 14 October, 14:00–16:00, in Harbour Room 3.

expected.action: Reply whether you will attend the Responsible AI roundtable

cases.subject: Venue changed: Responsible AI roundtable
cases.body: Hello, this is an important venue update for the Responsible AI roundtable. The date and time have not changed: the event will still take place on 14 October 2026 from 14:00 to 16:00. However, due to maintenance work near the original meeting room, we have moved the session from Harbour Room 3 to Gallery Hall 1 in the same building. Gallery Hall 1 is on the ground floor beside the main reception desk, and signs will be placed near the entrance. All existing registrations remain valid, so confirmed participants do not need to register again or reply to this update. The refreshments planned for 13:45 will also be available at the new location. If you previously declined the invitation, this venue change does not alter your response. Please use the new location in your calendar or travel notes to avoid going to the closed room. The event topic, speakers, and finish time remain unchanged. Contact the events team only if the new room creates an accessibility concern.
cases.summary: The 14 October Responsible AI roundtable is still 14:00–16:00 but has moved from Harbour Room 3 to Gallery Hall 1. Registrations remain valid.

cases.subject: Case CS-1047 resolved: repository access restored
cases.body: Hello Alex, this is the final update for help-desk case CS-1047 concerning access to the Project NOVA code repository. Our administrator found that the team group had been created correctly but had not been applied to the repository after the most recent permissions update. The group has now been refreshed, and repository access has been restored for both Alex and Sam. We confirmed that the two accounts can reach the project page and that the expected read and write permissions are present. You may need to sign out and back in, or refresh an existing browser session, before the change appears. The case is now marked resolved, and there is no need to reply if access works normally. If either team member still receives a permission error, reopen CS-1047 within three business days and include the exact error message and approximate time. After that period, a new case may be created automatically. This fix only changes Project NOVA repository access; it does not change permissions for other workspaces, course systems, or personal accounts.
cases.summary: Case CS-1047 is resolved: Project NOVA repository access was restored for Alex and Sam. Reopen the case within three business days only if access still fails.

cases.subject: Agent Systems Weekly: evaluation patterns
cases.body: Welcome to this week's Agent Systems Weekly. Our main editorial looks at a common evaluation mistake: measuring whether a system produces a fluent answer without checking whether it retrieved the right evidence first. We compare simple identifier queries, broader semantic questions, and cases where several documents describe the same topic over time. A second article explores citation faithfulness and suggests manually checking whether each claim is actually supported by the source shown beside it. We also share a short guide to synthetic test data, including how to preserve realistic relationships between messages without publishing personal information. In the tools section, readers discuss lightweight lexical retrieval, embedding-based search, and when a hybrid approach may be useful. The issue closes with links to three public evaluation templates and a recording from last month's community call. This is a general informational newsletter. There is no deadline, registration requirement, or requested response. You can manage newsletter preferences using the link in your account profile, and you may simply ignore this edition if the topics are not relevant to your work.
cases.summary: Agent Systems Weekly covers retrieval evaluation, citation faithfulness, and synthetic test data. It is informational and requires no action.

cases.subject: Coffee after Thursday's AX4102 class?
cases.body: Hi, I realised we have both been leaving AX4102 at about the same time on Thursday evenings, so I wanted to ask whether you would like to get coffee after class this week. I was thinking of the small café near the library because it stays open later than the one beside Studio B, but I am happy to go somewhere else if that is easier. There is nothing formal to discuss; it would just be nice to catch up and hear how your team project is going. I may need a few minutes after class to return some equipment, so around 21:40 would probably work. If you already have plans, please do not rearrange anything. There is no urgency, and you can reply whenever convenient. Also, this message is only a personal invitation from me, not an AX4102 course announcement or a change to the class schedule. I am sending it through the university address simply because that is the contact I had saved. Hope the week is going well either way.
cases.summary: Jamie invites you for an optional coffee after Thursday's AX4102 class, around 21:40 near the library. No urgent reply is needed.
